skills.title: Name the three forms of water (liquid, solid ice, invisible water vapour) and where each is found on Earth
Explain that almost all of Earth's water is salty sea water and only a tiny part is fresh water we can use
Explain how water changes form in daily life (evaporation, condensation, freezing, melting) without disappearing

expectations: Water is found as a liquid (seas, oceans, rivers, lakes, ponds, under the ground), as a solid (ice, snow, glaciers) and as a gas (water vapour in the air, which we cannot see).
Almost all of Earth's water, about 97 out of every 100 parts, is salty sea water that we cannot drink.
Most of the little fresh water is frozen in ice and glaciers or lies under the ground; less than 1 part in 100 is in rivers, lakes and reachable ground water for us to use.
Water keeps changing form: it evaporates into vapour, condenses back into drops, freezes into ice and melts again; it is never destroyed.
Because usable fresh water is so little and is shared by everyone, we must not waste or dirty it.

misconceptions.belief: Most of Earth's water can be drunk, so water can never run short.
signs: Says there is so much water on Earth that it can never run out
Forgets that sea water is salty when asked how much water we can use
Thinks water shortage happens only because people are careless with taps

diagnostic.prompt_en: Imagine all of Earth's water poured into 100 buckets. About how many buckets could we easily drink from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Socho, Earth ka saara paani 100 baaltiyon mein bhar diya. Inmein se lagbhag kitni baaltiyon ka paani hum aaraam se pee sakte hain?

options.text: Less than one bucket; the rest is salty or frozen
About 90 buckets, since most water on Earth is clean
All 100 buckets, as long as we boil it first

remediation.representation: 100-box grid coloured blue for sea, white for ice, and one tiny sliver for usable fresh water
remediation.moveShape: Child colours the grid from a guess first, then recolours it with the real split; ask what surprised them

misconceptions.belief: Boiling sea water makes it fit to drink.
signs: Says 'just boil it' as the fix for salty water
Mixes up killing germs with removing salt

diagnostic.prompt_en: A ship's cook boils a pot of sea water for a long time. Is the water in the pot now fit to drink?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Jahaaz ka cook samudra ke paani ko der tak ubaalta hai. Kya ab bartan ka paani peene laayak ho gaya?

options.text: Yes; long boiling takes the salt out of the water
No; boiling kills germs, but the salt stays in
Yes; sea water has hardly any salt in it anyway

remediation.representation: Two-panel picture: steam rising from the pot leaves salt behind on the sides of the pot
remediation.moveShape: Contrast what boiling does to germs with what it does to salt; link to the salt-left-on-a-plate observation

misconceptions.belief: When a puddle or wet clothes dry, the water is destroyed or vanishes forever.
signs: Says 'the sun ate the water' or 'the water finished'
Says the water went into the ground even for clothes on a line
Cannot say where drying water goes

diagnostic.prompt_en: Wet clothes on a line are dry by evening. Where did the water go?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Rassi pe tange geele kapde shaam tak sookh gaye. Unka paani kahaan gaya?

options.text: The sun's heat destroyed it, so it is gone forever
It is still hiding deep inside the threads
It went into the air as invisible water vapour

remediation.representation: Animated arrow loop: wet cloth to invisible vapour in the air to cloud to rain to puddle
remediation.moveShape: Use the cold-glass drops as proof that vapour is really in the air; ask them to trace the loop back to the cloth

misconceptions.belief: Drops on the outside of a cold glass are water leaking through the glass.
signs: Says the glass is 'sweating' its own water
Says the water seeped through tiny holes in the steel or glass

diagnostic.prompt_en: A steel glass full of ice-cold water gets drops all over its outside. Where did those drops come from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Barf jaise thande paani se bhare steel ke glass ke bahar boondein aa gayi. Ye boondein kahaan se aayi?

options.text: Water vapour from the air turned into drops on it
The cold glass itself made new water on its surface
The cold water inside leaked out through the glass

remediation.representation: Side-by-side: a cold glass filled with coloured water whose outside drops stay clear
remediation.moveShape: Predict-observe with coloured ice water: if drops were leaks they would be coloured; resolve the surprise explicitly

items.prompt_en: Name the three forms of water and give one place where you can find each.
items.prompt_hi: Paani ke teen roop batao, aur har roop ke liye ek jagah batao jahaan woh milta hai.
items.answer: Liquid: rivers, seas, ponds, tap water. Solid: ice in the freezer, snow and glaciers on the Himalayas. Gas: invisible water vapour in the air.
hints: Invite them to think about the freezer, the sky and the tap
Point to the ice tray and to wet clothes drying on a line
Prompt: water can be a liquid, a solid like ___, or a gas called water ___
Assert: liquid water, solid ice and invisible water vapour are all the same water

verified.solverAnswer: Liquid (river), solid (ice, glacier), gas (water vapour in air)

items.prompt_en: Where is most of Earth's water found: in rivers, in seas and oceans, or in ponds and lakes?
items.prompt_hi: Earth ka sabse zyada paani kahaan hai: nadiyon mein, samudra aur mahasagar mein, ya taalab aur jheelon mein?
items.answer: In the seas and oceans; about 97 out of every 100 parts of Earth's water is salty sea water.
hints: Ask them to picture a globe and say which colour covers most of it
Point to how much of a world map is blue sea
Prompt: most of Earth's water is in the ___, and it is ___
Assert: almost all of Earth's water is salty sea water in the oceans

verified.solverAnswer: Seas and oceans (~97%)

items.prompt_en: Take a steel glass of ice-cold water from the fridge and wipe its outside dry. Predict first: after five minutes, will the outside stay dry or get wet? If it gets wet, where will that water come from?
items.prompt_hi: Fridge se barf jaise thande paani ka steel glass nikalo aur bahar se poochh ke sukha kar do. Pehle guess karo: paanch minute baad glass bahar se sukha rahega ya geela ho jayega? Agar geela hua, toh woh paani kahaan se aayega?
items.answer: The outside gets covered with tiny drops. They come from invisible water vapour in the air that turns back into liquid when it touches the cold glass (condensation); the water inside does not leak out.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason before anyone looks
Point to whether the glass has holes and whether the water inside goes down
Prompt: the air around us has invisible water ___ that turns into drops on something ___
Assert: the drops come from water vapour in the air condensing on the cold glass

verified.solverAnswer: Outside gets wet; water vapour from air condenses on the cold glass

items.prompt_en: Two equally wet handkerchiefs: one spread open in the sun, one folded up in a shady corner. Predict which one dries first, and where its water goes.
items.prompt_hi: Do barabar geele rumaal: ek dhoop mein khol ke phailaya, ek chhaanv wale kone mein tah karke rakha. Guess karo kaunsa pehle sookhega, aur uska paani kahaan jayega?
items.answer: The one spread open in the sun dries first; warmth and a bigger open surface make the water evaporate faster. The water goes into the air as invisible water vapour; it is not destroyed.
hints: Ask which place their mother chooses for drying clothes
Point to warmth and to how much of the cloth touches the air
Prompt: in the sun the water ___ faster and goes into the ___
Assert: the open hanky in the sun dries first; its water becomes vapour in the air

verified.solverAnswer: Open one in sun dries first; water evaporates into air as vapour

items.prompt_en: Stir two spoons of salt into half a cup of water, pour it into a plate and leave it in the sun for two or three days. Predict: what will be left on the plate?
items.prompt_hi: Aadhe cup paani mein do chammach namak ghol do, plate mein daal ke do-teen din dhoop mein rakh do. Guess karo: plate mein kya bachega?
items.answer: The water evaporates and white salt is left behind on the plate. This is how salt is made from sea water in salt pans, for example in Gujarat.
hints: Ask what they think the sun does to the water in the plate
Point to what was mixed in that cannot fly away into the air
Prompt: the water goes into the air, but the ___ stays behind
Assert: only the water evaporates; the salt is left, just like in salt pans

verified.solverAnswer: White salt crystals; water evaporates, salt stays

items.prompt_en: There is so much water on Earth, yet many towns in India run short of drinking water every summer. Why?
items.prompt_hi: Earth pe itna saara paani hai, phir bhi har garmi mein India ke kai shehron mein peene ka paani kam pad jaata hai. Aisa kyon?
items.answer: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water, and most of the fresh water is frozen ice or deep under the ground; only a tiny part is in rivers, lakes and wells we can reach, and very many people share it.
hints: Invite them to recall the 100-bucket picture
Point to how much of that water is salty and how much is frozen
Prompt: the water we can drink is only a ___ part, and ___ people share it
Assert: usable fresh water is a tiny part of all water, so it can run short

verified.solverAnswer: Most water is salty or frozen; usable fresh water is tiny, uneven, demand high in summer

items.prompt_en: Rain clouds get much of their water from the salty sea. So why is rain water not salty?
items.prompt_hi: Baarish ke baadal apna kaafi paani khaare samudra se lete hain. Phir baarish ka paani khaara kyon nahi hota?
items.answer: When sea water evaporates, only the water rises as vapour; the salt stays behind in the sea. So clouds and rain are fresh water.
hints: Ask what was left on the plate of salty water in the sun
Point to what goes up into the air and what stays down
Prompt: when sea water evaporates, the ___ stays in the sea
Assert: only the water evaporates, so clouds and rain are not salty

verified.solverAnswer: Evaporation leaves salt behind; only pure vapour rises and condenses

items.prompt_en: Compare the water in a glacier high in the Himalayas with the water in the Arabian Sea. How are they different, and which one is fresh water?
items.prompt_hi: Himalaya ke glacier ke paani aur Arabian Sea ke paani ki tulna karo. Dono mein kya farak hai, aur kaunsa meetha (fresh) paani hai?
items.answer: Glacier water is solid ice and fresh, not salty; sea water is liquid and salty. Glacier ice melts slowly and feeds rivers like the Ganga.
hints: Ask which form each water is in: solid or liquid
Point to taste: which one would be salty
Prompt: glacier ice is ___ water and sea water is ___ water
Assert: glacier ice is frozen fresh water; the sea is salty liquid water

verified.solverAnswer: Glacier is frozen fresh water; Arabian Sea is salty liquid; glacier is fresh

items.prompt_en: Where does the water in your home's tap or handpump come from? Trace it back as far as you can.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar ke nal ya handpump ka paani kahaan se aata hai? Jitna peeche tak jaa sako, utna batao.
items.answer: From fresh water: a river, lake or dam reservoir through pipes and a tank, or from water under the ground through a borewell, well or handpump. All of it first came from rain or melting snow.
hints: Invite them to start at the tap and walk backwards along the pipe
Point to the tank on the roof or the pump in the ground
Prompt: the tank is filled from a ___ or from water under the ___
Assert: tap water comes from rivers, lakes or ground water, which come from rain and snow

verified.solverAnswer: Rain -> river/lake/groundwater -> reservoir/borewell -> pipe/pump -> tap

items.prompt_en: Chennai is right next to the sea, yet it sometimes faces water shortage. The city has built big plants that remove salt from sea water. Why can't every city just do this instead of saving water?
items.prompt_hi: Chennai bilkul samudra ke paas hai, phir bhi wahaan kabhi-kabhi paani ki kami hoti hai. Shehar ne bade plant banaye hain jo samudra ke paani se namak nikaalte hain. Har shehar bas yahi kyon nahi kar leta, paani bachane ki jagah?
items.answer: Removing salt from sea water needs big machines and a lot of electricity, so it is costly; it cannot replace saving water and keeping rivers, lakes and ground water clean.
hints: Ask what it would take to pull salt out of a whole river's worth of water
Point to the machines and the electricity such a plant needs
Prompt: removing salt is possible but very ___ and uses a lot of ___
Assert: desalting is costly and energy-hungry, so saving fresh water still matters

verified.solverAnswer: Desalination costs a lot of energy/money, needs coast, brine waste; saving water is cheaper

items.prompt_en: Draw 100 small boxes to stand for all of Earth's water. Colour how many are salty sea water, how many are frozen ice, and how many are fresh water we can use. Then tell me what your drawing shows.
items.prompt_hi: 100 chhote dabbe banao jo Earth ke saare paani ko dikhayein. Rang bharo: kitne dabbe khaara samudra, kitne jami hui barf, aur kitne woh meetha paani jo hum use kar sakte hain. Phir batao tumhari drawing kya dikhati hai.
items.answer: About 97 boxes for salty sea water, about 2 boxes for ice and glaciers, and less than 1 box shared by ground water, rivers and lakes; usable fresh water is a tiny part.
hints: Invite them to colour their guess first
Point to the sea: ask whether it takes a few boxes or nearly all of them
Prompt: after 97 sea boxes and about 2 ice boxes, the water we can use is less than ___ box
Assert: 97 salty, about 2 frozen, less than 1 usable fresh

verified.solverAnswer: About 97 salty, ~2 ice, ~1 usable fresh (<1)
verified.note: RESOLVED: h2 no longer states 97.

items.prompt_en: Pinky says: 'When a puddle dries in the sun, the water is finished forever. The sun destroys it.' What is wrong with Pinky's idea?
items.prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai: 'Jab dhoop mein gaddhe ka paani sookh jaata hai, toh paani hamesha ke liye khatam ho jaata hai. Suraj use mita deta hai.' Pinky ki baat mein galti kya hai?
items.answer: The water is not destroyed. It evaporates into the air as invisible water vapour, which later cools into clouds and comes back down as rain.
acceptable: bhaap ban ke hawa mein jaata hai
baarish ban ke wapas aata hai
hints: Ask where the drops on the cold glass came from
Point to the air above the puddle
Prompt: the puddle water turns into water ___ and later becomes ___
Assert: evaporating water goes into the air and returns as rain; it is never destroyed

verified.solverAnswer: Water not destroyed; evaporates into vapour in air, returns as rain

items.prompt_en: Your little cousin thinks steam, ice and rain are three totally different things. Explain to him how they are all water, and why we must not waste fresh water.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota cousin sochta hai ki bhaap, barf aur baarish teen bilkul alag cheezein hain. Use samjhao ki ye sab paani hi hain, aur hume meetha paani barbaad kyon nahi karna chahiye.
items.answer: Ice (solid), liquid water and water vapour (gas) are the same water in different forms; cooling and warming change the form. Very little of Earth's water is fresh and usable, so saving it matters.
hints: Invite them to start with an ice cube melting in a glass
Point to the three forms and what changes one into another
Prompt: ice, water and vapour are the same ___; only the ___ changes
Assert: they are one water in three forms, and usable fresh water is very little

verified.solverAnswer: Same water in three forms; fresh water scarce so save it

items.prompt_en: Quick one from last time: out of every 100 buckets of Earth's water, about how many are salty?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se ek jaldi wala sawaal: Earth ke har 100 baalti paani mein se lagbhag kitni baaltiyaan khaari hain?
items.answer: About 97.
hints: Ask them to picture the coloured 100-box drawing
Point to the big blue part
Prompt: it is more than 90, close to ___
Assert: about 97 out of 100 parts are salty sea water

verified.solverAnswer: About 97

workedExample.problem: A school uniform washed at night is dry by morning. Explain, step by step, where the water went.
steps: Notice: at night the uniform was heavy and wet; in the morning it is light and dry
Most of the water turned into invisible water vapour: this is evaporation
Moving air and warmth make evaporation go faster
The vapour mixes into the air; it is still water, now as a gas
Later, vapour cools high up into tiny drops that make clouds, and comes down again as rain

skills.title: Explain that plants take in water mainly through their roots and move it up the stem to the leaves
Explain how animals and humans get water (drinking, food) and lose it (sweat, breath, urine)
Explain why living things cannot survive without water and how desert plants and animals save water

expectations: Plants take in water mostly through their roots from the soil; the water travels up the stem to the leaves.
Plants use water, air and sunlight to make their own food in their leaves; soil gives water and some minerals, not ready-made food.
Leaves give out water vapour into the air through tiny openings.
Animals and people get water by drinking and from their food; more than half of our body is water, and we lose water through sweat, breath and urine.
Without water plants wilt and animals fall sick; desert plants and animals like the camel have special ways to save water.

misconceptions.belief: Plants drink water only through their leaves.
signs: Sprinkles water only on the leaves of a drooping plant
Says leaves drink the rain
Never mentions roots when asked how a plant gets water

diagnostic.prompt_en: A potted tulsi plant is drooping on a hot day. What is the best way to help it?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Garmi ke din gamle ka tulsi ka paudha murjha raha hai. Uski madad karne ka sabse achha tareeka kya hai?

options.text: Mix sugar into the soil so it gets some food
Pour water into the soil around its roots
Spray water only on its leaves, where it drinks

remediation.representation: Cut-away pot diagram with arrows from the soil into the roots and up the stem
remediation.moveShape: Run the coloured-water stem observation, then have the child trace the colour's path from bottom to top

misconceptions.belief: Plants get their food from the soil.
signs: Calls soil or manure 'plant food'
Says plants eat through their roots
Is surprised that a big tree did not use up the soil it stands in

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where does a mango tree get its food from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Aam ka ped apna khaana kahaan se laata hai?

options.text: It soaks up ready-made food from rain through its leaves
It takes ready-made food out of the soil with its roots
It makes it in its leaves with sunlight, water and air

remediation.representation: Leaf 'kitchen' picture: sunlight, water from the roots and air going in; food coming out
remediation.moveShape: Ask what goes into the leaf kitchen; contrast it with what the roots take from the soil

misconceptions.belief: A camel stores water in its hump.
signs: Calls the hump a water tank or water bottle
Explains desert survival only by the hump

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is stored inside a camel's hump?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Oont ke kubad mein kya bhara hota hai?

options.text: Fat, which its body can use when food is scarce
Extra water to drink later, like a water bottle
Nothing at all, because camels never need water

remediation.representation: Camel body cut-away: hump labelled fat; water held in the blood and body
remediation.moveShape: Contrast hump-as-tank with the real ways a camel saves water; let the child relabel the picture

misconceptions.belief: Some animals, like camels or desert lizards, do not need water at all.
signs: Says camels never drink
Says desert animals live without any water

diagnostic.prompt_en: A camel walks for days in the Thar desert without drinking. Does it need water?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Oont Thar ke registan mein kai din bina paani piye chalta hai. Kya use paani ki zaroorat hoti hai?

options.text: No; camels are desert animals and never need water
Yes; it drinks a lot at once and loses water slowly
Yes, and it sips from the water stored in its hump

remediation.representation: Water in and water out meter for a camel versus a buffalo
remediation.moveShape: Show both animals' water-in and water-out bars; ask why the camel's out-bar is so small

items.prompt_en: Through which part does a plant mostly take in water: its flowers, its leaves or its roots?
items.prompt_hi: Paudha zyaadatar paani kis hisse se leta hai: phoolon se, pattiyon se ya jadon se?
items.answer: Through its roots.
hints: Ask which part of the plant is inside the wet soil
Point to the part hidden under the ground
Prompt: water from the soil enters the plant through its ___
Assert: plants take in water mostly through their roots

verified.solverAnswer: Roots

items.prompt_en: Name three ways your body loses water in a day.
items.prompt_hi: Teen tareeke batao jinse tumhare shareer se din bhar mein paani nikalta hai.
items.answer: Sweating, breathing out water vapour, and passing urine (tears too).
hints: Ask what happens to their shirt after running in the sun
Point to breathing on a cold mirror
Prompt: we lose water through ___, through our ___ and when we go to the toilet
Assert: sweat, breath and urine all take water out of our body

verified.solverAnswer: Urine, sweat, breath, stool

items.prompt_en: Put a white flower (like a white rose or guldaudi) or a leafy stem in a glass of water with a few drops of food colour. Ask an adult to cut the stem fresh. Predict: what will you see on the petals or leaves after a day?
items.prompt_hi: Ek safed phool (jaise safed gulab ya guldaudi) ya patton wali tehni ko paani ke glass mein rakho jismein khaane ka rang ki kuch boondein daali hon. Tehni kisi bade se taaza katwa lo. Guess karo: ek din baad pankhudiyon ya pattiyon pe kya dikhega?
items.answer: The colour shows up in the petals or in the veins of the leaves, because water travels up the stem from the bottom to the top.
hints: Ask for a guess before the glass is set up
Point to where the stem touches the coloured water
Prompt: the coloured water will travel ___ the stem to the ___
Assert: water moves up from the bottom of the stem to the petals and leaves

verified.solverAnswer: Petals/leaves take colour of dye (coloured veins)

items.prompt_en: In the morning, tie a clear plastic bag around one leafy branch of a plant standing in the sun (only the branch, not the whole plant). Predict: what will you see inside the bag by evening?
items.prompt_hi: Subah dhoop mein khade paudhe ki ek patton wali daal pe saaf plastic ki thaili baandh do (sirf daal pe, poore paudhe pe nahi). Guess karo: shaam tak thaili ke andar kya dikhega?
items.answer: Water drops and mist inside the bag. The leaves give out water vapour through tiny openings, and it turns into drops on the bag; this water came up from the roots.
hints: Ask whether the bag will stay dry or not, and why
Point to the cold glass drops from last time
Prompt: leaves give out water ___ that turns into ___ on the bag
Assert: leaves breathe out water vapour, which collects as drops inside the bag

verified.solverAnswer: Water droplets/mist on inside of bag (transpiration)

items.prompt_en: Two drooping potted plants: for one you spray water only on the leaves; for the other you pour water into the soil. Predict which one will stand up straight first.
items.prompt_hi: Do murjhaye hue gamle ke paudhe: ek ki sirf pattiyon pe paani chhidko, doosre ki mitti mein paani daalo. Guess karo kaunsa paudha pehle seedha khada hoga.
items.answer: The one watered in the soil, because its roots take up the water and send it up the stem to the leaves.
acceptable: the one watered in the soil
hints: Ask which part of the plant drinks
Point to where the roots are
Prompt: water must reach the ___ to travel up to the leaves
Assert: the soil-watered plant recovers first because roots take in the water

verified.solverAnswer: Soil-watered plant recovers first (roots absorb)

items.prompt_en: Why does a plant droop (wilt) if it gets no water for a few days?
items.prompt_hi: Agar paudhe ko kuch din paani na mile, toh woh murjha kyon jaata hai?
items.answer: Water keeps the stem and leaves firm and is needed to make food. Without water coming up from the roots, the leaves lose more water than they get, go soft and droop.
acceptable: paani se paudha tight rehta hai
hints: Ask what a balloon looks like with and without air in it
Point to water filling the plant like air fills the balloon
Prompt: without water, the stem and leaves become ___ and ___
Assert: water keeps the plant firm; without it, the plant goes soft and wilts

verified.solverAnswer: Cells lose water, stems lose firmness; water not replaced

items.prompt_en: Farmers add manure to the soil. So does a plant eat soil and manure as its food? Explain.
items.prompt_hi: Kisaan mitti mein khaad daalte hain. Toh kya paudha mitti aur khaad ko apna khaana bana ke khaata hai? Samjhao.
items.answer: No. A plant makes its own food in its leaves using sunlight, water and air. Its roots take water and small amounts of minerals from the soil and manure, which keep it healthy, but soil is not its food.
acceptable: no, it makes its own food
hints: Ask what a plant kept in a dark room for a week looks like
Point to the leaves and the sunlight they need
Prompt: the leaf makes food from sunlight, ___ and ___
Assert: plants make their food in leaves; soil gives water and minerals, not food

verified.solverAnswer: No; plant makes its own food in leaves from sunlight, water, CO2; soil gives water and minerals

items.prompt_en: Compare a camel in the Thar desert with a buffalo near a village pond. How does each manage its water?
items.prompt_hi: Thar registan ke oont aur gaon ke taalab ke paas wali bhains ki tulna karo. Dono apne paani ka intezaam kaise karte hain?
items.answer: The buffalo drinks often and lies in the pond to stay cool. The camel can go many days without drinking because its body loses very little water, and it drinks a lot at once when it finds water. Its hump stores fat, not water.
acceptable: camel saves water, buffalo drinks often
hints: Ask how often each animal can find water where it lives
Point to how little the camel sweats and how much it drinks at once
Prompt: the buffalo drinks ___, while the camel's body loses water very ___
Assert: the buffalo depends on the pond; the camel saves water, and its hump is fat

verified.solverAnswer: Camel: saves water, loses little, drinks lots at once, fat in hump; buffalo drinks often, wallows

items.prompt_en: On a hot summer day you play cricket for two hours. What happens to the water in your body, and what should you do?
items.prompt_hi: Garmi ke din tum do ghante cricket khelte ho. Tumhare shareer ke paani ka kya hota hai, aur tumhe kya karna chahiye?
items.answer: You lose a lot of water as sweat and through breathing, so you feel thirsty and tired. Drink water often and rest in the shade.
hints: Ask how their T-shirt looks after the match
Point to where that wetness came from
Prompt: sweating takes ___ out of the body, so we must ___
Assert: we lose water as sweat, so we must drink water and rest in shade

verified.solverAnswer: Lose water by sweat; drink water/ORS, rest in shade

items.prompt_en: Many farmers in Rajasthan use drip irrigation: thin pipes drip water right at the base of each plant. Why is this smarter than flooding the whole field with water?
items.prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke kai kisaan drip irrigation use karte hain: patli pipe se paani boond-boond har paudhe ki jad ke paas girta hai. Ye poore khet mein paani bhar dene se zyada samajhdaari kyon hai?
items.answer: The water goes straight to the roots, where the plant takes it in, so less water is lost to evaporation or to soil where there are no roots. It saves scarce water.
hints: Ask where the plant actually takes in water
Point to the open wet ground between plants in a flooded field
Prompt: drip pipes put water right at the ___, so less is ___
Assert: drip irrigation feeds the roots directly and wastes far less water

verified.solverAnswer: Drip gives water at roots, little evaporation/runoff, saves water

skills.title: Name where rivers begin (glaciers, springs, lakes, rain on hills) and where they end (sea, lake or a bigger river)

expectations: A river begins at its source, high up: a melting glacier, a spring, a lake, or rain collecting on hills and mountains.
Water always flows downhill, so a river flows from high land to lower land and finally into a sea, a lake or a bigger river (its mouth).
Smaller rivers called tributaries join the main river on the way and make it bigger.
In the mountains a river is narrow and fast and cuts valleys; in the plains it slows, spreads out and drops fine, fertile soil called silt.
People settle along rivers for water, farming, fishing and travel; the Godavari, for example, starts in the hills near Nashik and flows east across India into the Bay of Bengal.

hints: Ask for a guess about the direction before pouring
Point to the highest and the lowest point of the sand hill
Prompt: water always flows from ___ places to ___ places
Assert: water runs downhill and carries soil, just like a river from mountain to sea

verified.solverAnswer: Downhill; carries soil/sand

items.prompt_en: A river rushes down a steep mountain and then reaches flat plains. Predict: in the plains, will it flow faster or slower, and what will happen to the mud it is carrying?
items.prompt_hi: Ek nadi oonche pahad se tezi se neeche aati hai aur phir samatal maidaan mein pahunchti hai. Guess karo: maidaan mein woh tez bahegi ya dheere, aur jo mitti woh saath laa rahi hai uska kya hoga?
items.answer: Slower. As it slows down, it drops the fine mud and sand (silt) it was carrying, which makes the land in the plains fertile.

items.prompt_en: The Ganga flows into the sea every day. Why does it not run out of water?
items.prompt_hi: Ganga roz samudra mein behti hai. Phir uska paani khatam kyon nahi hota?
items.answer: Rain and melting snow and glacier ice in the Himalayas keep feeding it, and tributaries add more. Water from the sea evaporates and comes back as rain, so it is a cycle.

items.prompt_en: Why have so many big towns and cities, like Varanasi, Patna and Rajahmundry, grown up on river banks?

Point to the farms, boats and fish near a river
Prompt: rivers give people ___, good soil for ___ and a way to travel
Assert: towns grow by rivers for water, farming, fish and trade

items.prompt_en: Compare a river high in the mountains with the same river near the sea. Think about its speed, its width and the land around it.

items.answer: In the mountains it is narrow, fast and rocky and cuts deep valleys. Near the sea it is wide and slow, flows over flat land, drops silt and may split into many channels (a delta).

items.prompt_en: Is there a river, nala or stream near your town? Ask an elder where it begins and where it ends. Is the start higher or lower than the end?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar ke paas koi nadi, naala ya dhaara hai? Kisi bade se poochho ki woh kahaan se shuru hoti hai aur kahaan khatam. Shuru wali jagah oonchi hai ya khatam wali?

items.answer: The water flows downhill from higher to lower places; small streams join into bigger ones like tributaries; it carries mud and leaves; and it ends in a bigger drain or river, like a river reaching the sea.

expectations: Floods happen when more water comes than a river, drain or the ground can hold: very heavy rain, overflowing rivers and blocked drains.
Tree roots and grass hold the soil and help rain soak into the ground; when forests are cut, rain runs off fast with mud and floods come quicker.
Rivers get dirty from sewage, factory waste, garbage, plastic, soap, and idols made of plaster of Paris and harmful paints.
A river cannot clean itself of everything: plastic and harmful chemicals stay and hurt fish, animals and people downstream.

We can help by keeping garbage and plastic out of water, using clay idols and immersion tanks, keeping drains clear and planting trees; in a flood, stay away from flowing water and follow official warnings.

items.prompt_en: Find a small slope in a park or garden with one grassy patch and one bare patch of soil. Pour one mug of water at the top of each. Predict: which patch will send down more muddy water, and faster?

skills.title: Name traditional (sun-drying, salting, sugar, oil, pickling) and modern (fridge, freezing, boiling milk, airtight packets and cans) ways of preserving food

expectations: Preserving food means keeping it from spoiling for longer by stopping or slowing microbes.

Drying (papad, vadi, dried fish, raisins) removes the water microbes need; a lot of salt (achaar) or sugar (murabba, jam) pulls water out so microbes cannot grow easily; a layer of oil keeps air and moisture away.
A fridge only slows microbes down; it does not kill them, so food in the fridge also spoils after some days. Freezing slows them much more.
Boiling milk or cooking kills many microbes; airtight packets and cans keep new microbes out.
Always check the smell, the look and the expiry date on packets, and never taste food to test whether it has spoiled.

skills.title: Identify ways visitors can harm fragile places: litter and plastic, noise, feeding animals, touching coral, collecting shells, plucking plants, leaving paths, scratching walls
Suggest responsible behaviour for tourists and local people that protects a place
Explain how many small actions by many visitors add up to big harm or big help

expectations: Fragile places like coral reefs, forests, hills, beaches and old monuments can be harmed by visitors even when they do not mean to.
Harm comes from litter and plastic, loud noise, feeding or chasing wild animals, plucking plants, touching or standing on coral, collecting shells, leaving the paths, and scratching walls.
One small careless act repeated by thousands of visitors becomes big damage.
Responsible visitors carry their waste back, use refillable bottles and cloth bags, stay on paths, keep quiet near animals, never feed wildlife, and follow local rules and guides.
Local people protect these places too, and visitors should respect their homes, culture and rules.

misconceptions.belief: Visiting a place cannot harm it.
signs: Says 'we are only tourists, we can't hurt anything'
Sees no harm in walking on coral or scratching names on walls

diagnostic.prompt_en: Every year thousands of tourists walk on a coral reef at low tide. What happens?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Har saal hazaaron tourist low tide pe coral reef ke upar chalte hain. Kya hota hai?

options.text: The coral grows faster because it gets touched
The living coral breaks and dies; fish lose homes
Nothing; walking on coral does not hurt it at all

remediation.representation: Before and after picture of a reef path: colourful corals versus broken grey rubble
remediation.moveShape: Remind them corals are animals; ask what a thousand footsteps would do to any living thing

misconceptions.belief: One small wrapper or bottle does not matter.
signs: Says 'it's just one'
Leaves a wrapper where others are already lying

diagnostic.prompt_en: On a popular trek trail, each of 10,000 trekkers in a season drops 'just one' wrapper. What does the trail look like at the end of the season?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek mashhoor trek raaste pe ek season mein 10,000 trekker 'bas ek' wrapper giraate hain. Season ke aakhir mein raasta kaisa dikhega?

options.text: Clean; the wind will blow all of them away
Still clean, because one wrapper each is nothing
Thousands of wrappers pile up and harm animals

remediation.representation: Multiplier strip: 1 wrapper times 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000 visitors, drawn as growing piles
remediation.moveShape: Child does the multiplying; ask whose 'just one' it was in the big pile

misconceptions.belief: Feeding wild animals is kind and helps them.
signs: Throws chips or biscuits to monkeys or ducks
Says the animals look hungry, so feeding them is good

diagnostic.prompt_en: Monkeys on a hill road look hungry. What is the kind thing to do?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Pahadi sadak pe bandar bhookhe lag rahe hain. Sabse samajhdaari aur dayaa wala kaam kya hai?

options.text: Don't feed them; human food makes them sick
Feed them chips and biscuits, since they're hungry
Feed them only bread, because bread is healthy

remediation.representation: Two-path story: monkeys finding forest food versus monkeys waiting at the roadside for snacks
remediation.moveShape: Follow both paths for a few months; ask which monkeys stay healthy and wild

items.prompt_en: Name three ways tourists can harm a hill station or a forest.
items.prompt_hi: Teen tareeke batao jinse tourist kisi hill station ya jungle ko nuksaan pahuncha sakte hain.
items.answer: Any three: dropping litter and plastic, loud music and noise, feeding or chasing animals, plucking plants and flowers, leaving the paths, scratching rocks and trees, careless fires.
hints: Ask what they have seen people leave behind at picnic spots
Point to the animals and plants that live there
Prompt: tourists can leave ___, make loud ___, or feed ___
Assert: litter, noise, feeding animals and plucking plants all harm a place

verified.solverAnswer: Litter, noise, feeding animals, damaging plants, building

items.prompt_en: Name three things you would carry or do on a trek so that you leave no trash behind.
items.prompt_hi: Trek pe teen cheezein batao jo tum saath le jaoge ya karoge taaki koi kachra peeche na chhoote.
items.answer: Any three: carry a refillable steel bottle, take a cloth bag for snacks and for bringing wrappers back, avoid packaged food, and put all waste back in your bag to throw in a bin at home or in town.
hints: Ask what usually becomes trash on a trek
Point to bottles and wrappers
Prompt: carry a ___ bottle and a bag to bring your ___ back
Assert: refillable bottle, cloth bag, less packaging, and carry all waste back

verified.solverAnswer: Cloth bag, reusable bottle, bring trash back, avoid plastic

items.prompt_en: Predict first: if each of 5,000 visitors to a waterfall leaves just one plastic bottle in a season, what will the area look like by the end? Then work out how many bottles that is.
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: agar ek jharne pe aane waale 5,000 log ek season mein bas ek-ek plastic bottle chhod dein, toh season ke aakhir tak wahaan ka haal kaisa hoga? Phir hisaab lagao kitni bottlein hui.
items.answer: 5,000 bottles. Heaps of plastic would choke the stream, spoil its beauty and harm fish and animals; small acts add up.
hints: Ask for a picture guess before the number
Point to one bottle times 5,000 people
Prompt: 1 bottle times 5,000 visitors is ___ bottles
Assert: 5,000 bottles; many small acts make a big mess

verified.solverAnswer: 5000 bottles; littered area

items.prompt_en: At a hill station, tourists feed monkeys chips every day. Predict how the monkeys will behave after a few months.
items.prompt_hi: Ek hill station pe tourist roz bandaron ko chips khilaate hain. Guess karo kuch mahino baad bandar kaisa bartaav karenge.
items.answer: They stop looking for their natural food and depend on people; they snatch bags and food, may bite, and can fall sick from salty, fried food.
hints: Ask what anyone does when free snacks keep coming
Point to bags that smell of chips
Prompt: the monkeys will stop finding forest food and start ___ from people
Assert: fed monkeys become dependent, bold and unhealthy

verified.solverAnswer: Monkeys depend on food, become bold/aggressive, snatch

items.prompt_en: Predict: if everyone takes a shortcut across a grassy hill slope instead of using the path, what will the slope look like after one monsoon?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar sab log raaste ki jagah ghaas wali pahadi dhalaan se shortcut lein, toh ek monsoon ke baad dhalaan kaisi dikhegi?
items.answer: The grass gets trampled and dies, leaving bare soil; the rain then washes the soil away, cutting gullies and causing mud slides.
acceptable: grass dies and soil washes away
ghaas mar jayegi, mitti beh jayegi
hints: Ask what happens to grass on a cricket pitch's crease
Point to the bare soil and the rain
Prompt: trampled grass ___, and rain washes the ___ away
Assert: shortcuts kill grass and let rain wash the slope away

verified.solverAnswer: Bare, eroded path/gullies, soil washes away

items.prompt_en: Why do forest guards ask visitors to stay on the marked path and keep quiet?
items.prompt_hi: Jungle ke guard tourists ko nishaan wale raaste pe rehne aur shaant rehne ko kyon kehte hain?
items.answer: Paths protect plants and soil from trampling; noise scares animals and disturbs their feeding and nesting; staying on paths also keeps visitors safe.
hints: Ask how a bird on its nest feels when people shout nearby
Point to plants beside the path
Prompt: paths protect the ___, and quiet protects the ___
Assert: paths save plants and soil, quiet saves animals, and both keep us safe

verified.solverAnswer: Protect plants, avoid disturbing animals, avoid fire/trampling

items.prompt_en: Compare two tourist groups at a beach in Lakshadweep. Group A collects shells and pieces of coral as souvenirs and leaves wrappers behind. Group B takes only photos and carries its waste back. What does each leave for the next visitors?
items.prompt_hi: Lakshadweep ke beach pe do tourist groups ki tulna karo. Group A yaadgaar ke liye seepiyaan aur coral ke tukde le jaata hai aur wrapper chhod deta hai. Group B sirf photo leta hai aur apna kachra wapas le jaata hai. Har group agle logon ke liye kya chhodta hai?
items.answer: Group A leaves fewer shells and less coral, so hermit crabs and fish lose homes, plus litter; taking coral is also against the law in India. Group B leaves the beach clean and alive for everyone who comes next.
hints: Ask who lives inside empty shells on a beach
Point to the wrappers left behind
Prompt: Group A takes away animal ___ and leaves ___
Assert: Group B protects the beach; Group A harms it even on a short visit

verified.solverAnswer: A leaves damaged beach, trash; B leaves clean beach

items.prompt_en: Your school is going on a picnic to a park with a lake. Make three rules for your class so the park stays as nice as it was.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara school ek jheel wale park mein picnic pe ja raha hai. Apni class ke liye teen niyam banao taaki park waisa hi achha rahe jaisa tha.
items.answer: Any three: no littering and carry waste back, do not feed the ducks or fish junk food, do not pluck flowers, stay on the paths, no loud music, keep the lake water clean.
hints: Ask what would spoil the park for the next class
Point to the lake, the plants and the birds
Prompt: rule one is about ___, rule two about animals, rule three about ___
Assert: carry waste back, don't feed wildlife, protect plants and water

verified.solverAnswer: Do not litter, do not pick plants, stay on paths, no feeding animals

items.prompt_en: An old fort near your town has names scratched on its walls. Why is this harmful, and what could your class do about it?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare shehar ke paas ek purane kile ki deewaron pe naam khurche hue hain. Ye nuksaandeh kyon hai, aur tumhari class iske liye kya kar sakti hai?
items.answer: Scratching damages a monument that can never be replaced and spoils history for everyone. The class could make posters, talk to visitors, report damage to the caretakers or the Archaeological Survey of India, and never scratch walls themselves.
hints: Ask how old the fort is and whether it can be rebuilt the same
Point to how many visitors come each year
Prompt: old walls cannot be ___, so the class can make ___ to warn visitors
Assert: monuments are irreplaceable; spread the word and report damage

verified.solverAnswer: Damages heritage; class campaign, signs

items.prompt_en: Make a 'Visitor Code' poster for the Western Ghats with four pictures and one short line each.
items.prompt_hi: Western Ghats ke liye ek 'Visitor Code' poster banao jismein chaar tasveerein hon aur har ek ke saath ek chhoti line.
items.answer: Four clear rules, for example: carry back your waste; never feed animals; stay on the trail; use a refillable bottle; keep music off; respect local rules.
hints: Invite them to pick the four harms they think are worst
Point to turning each harm into a do-this picture
Prompt: a picture of a bottle could say 'use a ___ bottle'
Assert: four simple picture rules that turn harms into good habits

verified.solverAnswer: Poster four pictures

items.prompt_en: Bunty says, 'We are only tourists. We come for two days and go. How can we harm the place?' What would you tell him?
items.prompt_hi: Bunty kehta hai, 'Hum toh bas tourist hain. Do din ke liye aate hain aur chale jaate hain. Hum jagah ko kaise nuksaan pahuncha sakte hain?' Tum use kya bologe?
items.answer: Each visitor's waste, noise and damage add up with thousands of others; even a short visit can leave litter, scare animals, and break coral and plants.
hints: Ask how many tourists visit in a year
Point to the 'just one wrapper' pile
Prompt: one visitor is small, but ___ visitors together make big ___
Assert: short visits by many people add up to real harm

verified.solverAnswer: Many tourists add up; small harms add up

items.prompt_en: Before your family's trip to the hills, explain to your cousin how tourists can harm a place and three things your family will do to protect it.
items.prompt_hi: Family ke pahadon wale trip se pehle apne cousin ko samjhao ki tourist kisi jagah ko kaise nuksaan pahunchaate hain, aur tumhari family use bachaane ke liye teen kya kaam karegi.
items.answer: Harm comes from litter, noise, feeding animals, plucking plants and leaving paths, and many small acts add up. Family actions: carry waste back, use steel bottles and cloth bags, stay on paths, keep quiet near animals, never feed wildlife, follow local rules.
hints: Invite them to start with one harm they have seen
Point to how small acts multiply
Prompt: we will carry our ___ back, stay on ___, and never ___ animals
Assert: name the harms, explain how they add up, and commit to three protecting habits

verified.solverAnswer: Harm: litter, noise, damage; protect: carry trash back, stay on path, no feeding

items.prompt_en: From last time: why is 'just one wrapper' a problem in a popular place?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi mashhoor jagah pe 'bas ek wrapper' kyon pareshaani hai?
items.answer: Because thousands of visitors each leave 'just one', and together it becomes a huge pile of waste.
hints: Ask how many visitors such a place gets
Point to the multiplier strip
Prompt: one wrapper times ___ visitors is a huge ___
Assert: everyone's 'just one' adds up to a mountain of waste

verified.solverAnswer: One wrapper multiplied by many visitors; pollution lasts

skills.title: Say that energy is what is needed to make things move, work, heat up, light up or make sound, and that we see what energy does, not energy itself
Name sources of energy (food, sun, wind, flowing water, fuels, electricity) and match them to what they make work
Trace energy chains, such as sun to plant to food to our body, or wind, water, coal or sunlight to electricity to a fan

expectations: Energy is needed for anything to move, work, grow, heat up, light up or make sound; we cannot see energy itself, only what it does.
Our body gets energy from food; plants use sunlight to make their food, so the energy in our food first came from the Sun.

Wind moves kites, sailboats and windmills; flowing water turns water wheels and turbines; fuels such as petrol, diesel, LPG, coal and wood give energy when burnt; electricity runs fans, lights and machines.
Electricity is itself made from other sources, such as burning coal, falling water, wind and sunlight.
Energy is not used up into nothing; it changes from one form to another, for example electricity into light and heat in a bulb.

misconceptions.belief: Energy is a substance you can see or hold.
signs: Points to petrol or a battery and says 'that is energy'
Draws energy as a liquid or a glowing ball

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these is the best way to describe energy?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Energy ko samjhaane ka sabse sahi tareeka inmein se kaunsa hai?

options.text: A liquid or powder you can see inside batteries
Something unseen that makes things move, glow or heat
Only something that comes out of a wall plug

remediation.representation: Effects board: pictures of moving, lighting, heating and sound, each labelled 'energy at work'
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to point to the energy in each picture; resolve that they are pointing to what energy does

misconceptions.belief: Only electricity, or only machines and living things, have energy; wind, moving balls or sunlight do not.
signs: Says wind or a rolling ball has no energy
Lists only plugged-in things when asked about energy

diagnostic.prompt_en: Does the wind that makes your kite fly have energy?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Jo hawa tumhari patang udaati hai, kya usmein energy hai?

options.text: No; only things plugged into electricity have it
No; only living things like us have energy
Yes; moving air has energy that can lift a kite

remediation.representation: Moving things gallery: kite, rolling ball, river, windmill, each with its push shown
remediation.moveShape: Run the bottle-knocking roll; ask what knocked the bottles over if not energy

misconceptions.belief: The energy in our food has nothing to do with the Sun.
signs: Says food energy comes from the cooking gas
Cannot link plants to sunlight when explaining food

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where did the energy in your roti first come from?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tumhari roti ki energy sabse pehle kahaan se aayi?

options.text: From sunlight that the wheat plant used for food
From the gas stove flame that cooked it
From the wheat flour itself, not from the Sun

remediation.representation: Energy chain cards: Sun, wheat plant, flour, roti, child running
remediation.moveShape: Child lines up the cards and says what passes along each arrow

misconceptions.belief: Electricity gets used up inside the bulb and does not come back to the battery.
signs: Draws current going only from the battery to the bulb and stopping
Thinks one wire is enough to light a bulb

diagnostic.prompt_en: In a torch, electric current flows from the battery through the bulb. What happens to the current?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Torch mein bijli ka current battery se bulb tak jaata hai. Phir current ka kya hota hai?

options.text: It leaks out of the hot bulb into the air
It flows round the loop and back to the battery
It gets used up in the bulb and stops there

remediation.representation: Animated torch circuit with dots flowing round a complete loop and the bulb glowing where energy is given out
remediation.moveShape: Contrast an open loop with a closed loop on screen; ask why the bulb needs both wires

items.prompt_en: What gives energy to each of these: a flying kite, a spinning ceiling fan, you running a race, a moving car?
items.prompt_hi: In sabko energy kahaan se milti hai: udti patang, ghoomta pankha, race mein daudte hue tum, aur chalti car?
items.answer: Kite: the wind. Fan: electricity. You: food. Car: fuel such as petrol, diesel or CNG, or electricity for an electric car.
hints: Ask what the kite needs on a still day
Point to the plug and the petrol pump
Prompt: kite ___, fan ___, you ___, car ___
Assert: wind, electricity, food and fuel

verified.solverAnswer: Kite: wind; fan: electricity; you: food; car: petrol/fuel

items.prompt_en: Name three things energy can do.
items.prompt_hi: Teen kaam batao jo energy kar sakti hai.
items.answer: Any three: make things move, make heat, give light, make sound, help living things grow.
hints: Ask what a bulb, a fan and a speaker each do
Point to warmth from the sun
Prompt: energy can make things ___, make ___ and give ___
Assert: energy moves, heats, lights, makes sound and helps growth

verified.solverAnswer: Make things move, give heat, light, sound, run machines

items.prompt_en: Make a paper pinwheel (firki) by folding paper; ask an adult if anything needs cutting. Hold it still in a room with no breeze, then in a breeze outside, then blow on it hard. Predict: when will it spin fastest?
items.prompt_hi: Kaagaz ko mod ke ek firki banao; kuch kaatna ho toh kisi bade se kehna. Pehle use bina hawa wale kamre mein pakdo, phir bahar hawa mein, phir zor se phoonk maaro. Guess karo: kab sabse tez ghoomegi?
items.answer: It does not spin in still air; it spins in the breeze and fastest when you blow hard, because stronger moving air has more energy to push it.
hints: Ask for a guess for each of the three tries
Point to what is different each time: how fast the air moves
Prompt: faster air has ___ energy, so the firki spins ___
Assert: moving air has energy; more speed, more energy, faster spin

verified.solverAnswer: In a hard blow/strong wind; hard blow fastest

items.prompt_en: Put a dark cloth and a white cloth side by side in the sun for 30 minutes. Predict: which one will feel warmer when you touch it?
items.prompt_hi: Ek gehre rang ka kapda aur ek safed kapda saath-saath 30 minute dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo: chhoone pe kaunsa zyada garam lagega?
items.answer: The dark cloth. It takes in more of the Sun's energy, which turns into heat; the white cloth reflects more of the sunlight.
hints: Ask which colour of T-shirt feels hotter in summer
Point to sunlight landing on both
Prompt: the dark cloth takes in more of the Sun's ___, which becomes ___
Assert: dark cloth absorbs more sunlight energy and gets warmer

verified.solverAnswer: Dark cloth warmer

items.prompt_en: Stand some empty plastic bottles in a row. Roll a ball gently at them, then roll it hard. Predict: which roll will knock down more bottles, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Kuch khaali plastic bottlein line mein khadi karo. Ek baar ball dheere se lurhkao, phir zor se. Guess karo: kis baar zyada bottlein girengi, aur kyon?
items.answer: The hard roll. A faster-moving ball has more energy, so it can push more bottles over. We do not see the energy itself; we see what it does.
hints: Ask for a guess before rolling
Point to the speed of the ball each time
Prompt: a ___ ball has more energy to knock things over
Assert: faster ball, more energy, more bottles knocked down

verified.solverAnswer: Hard roll knocks down more; more energy

items.prompt_en: We say the energy in your food came from the Sun. Explain how.
items.prompt_hi: Hum kehte hain ki tumhare khaane ki energy Suraj se aayi. Samjhao kaise.
items.answer: Plants use sunlight to make their own food and store it in their leaves, grains and fruits. We eat plants, or animals that ate plants, so the energy in our food started as sunlight.
acceptable: plants use sunlight to make food
paudhe dhoop se khaana banaate hain
hints: Ask what a wheat plant needs to grow
Point to the leaf as the plant's kitchen
Prompt: plants store the Sun's ___ in their food, and we ___ the plants
Assert: sunlight to plant food to our food: our energy began with the Sun

verified.solverAnswer: Plants use sunlight to make food; we eat plants or animals that eat plants

items.prompt_en: Why do you feel tired and hungry after playing football for an hour?
items.prompt_hi: Ek ghanta football khelne ke baad tum thake hue aur bhookhe kyon mehsoos karte ho?
items.answer: Your body used a lot of the energy it got from food to run and kick; it needs more food to get energy again.
hints: Ask where their body gets energy from
Point to all the running in the game
Prompt: playing used up the energy from ___, so the body wants more ___
Assert: running uses food energy, so we feel tired and hungry

verified.solverAnswer: Used energy from food; body needs to refill

items.prompt_en: Compare a pair of bullocks pulling a plough with a tractor pulling a plough. Where does each get its energy from?
items.prompt_hi: Hal kheenchte bailon ki jodi aur hal kheenchte tractor ki tulna karo. Dono ko energy kahaan se milti hai?
items.answer: The bullocks get energy from the grass and fodder they eat, which got its energy from the Sun. The tractor gets energy from diesel burnt in its engine. Both need energy to do the work.
acceptable: bullocks from food, tractor from diesel
bail chaare se, tractor diesel se
hints: Ask what each one 'eats'
Point to the grass and the fuel tank
Prompt: bullocks get energy from ___, the tractor from ___
Assert: food for the bullocks, diesel for the tractor; both need energy to plough

verified.solverAnswer: Bullocks: food/fodder (from sun via plants); tractor: diesel fuel

items.prompt_en: Trace where the energy for the fan in your room comes from, going back as many steps as you can.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare kamre ke pankhe ki energy kahaan se aati hai, jitne peeche ke steps tak jaa sako, utna batao.
items.answer: The fan runs on electricity that comes through wires from a power station. Much of India's electricity is made by burning coal; some comes from falling water at dams, from wind and from sunlight on solar panels. Coal formed long ago from plants, which got their energy from the Sun.
hints: Invite them to start at the switch and follow the wire
Point to power stations and what they burn or use
Prompt: fan, then ___, then power station that uses ___ or water or wind
Assert: fan to electricity to power station to coal, water, wind or sun

verified.solverAnswer: Power station (coal/hydro/wind/solar) -> wires -> house -> fan

items.prompt_en: In Tamil Nadu and Gujarat there are rows of tall windmills (wind turbines) near the coast. How do they help a family in a faraway city watch TV?
items.prompt_hi: Tamil Nadu aur Gujarat mein samudra ke paas lambi-lambi windmills (wind turbines) ki kataarein hain. Ye kisi door shehar ki family ko TV dekhne mein kaise madad karti hain?
items.answer: The wind turns the blades, which turn a generator that makes electricity; the electricity travels through wires to homes far away, where it runs the TV.
hints: Ask what the wind does to the blades
Point to the wires leaving the wind farm
Prompt: wind turns the ___, which makes ___ that travels through ___
Assert: wind energy becomes electricity, which travels to homes and runs the TV

verified.solverAnswer: Wind turns turbine, generates electricity sent via grid to cities

items.prompt_en: Draw an energy chain with arrows: Sun, wheat plant, roti, you, cycling to school. Write under each arrow what is happening.
items.prompt_hi: Teer ke saath ek energy chain banao: Suraj, gehoon ka paudha, roti, tum, school cycle se jaana. Har teer ke neeche likho kya ho raha hai.
items.answer: Sun to plant: the plant uses sunlight to make food. Plant to roti: wheat grain is ground and cooked into roti. Roti to you: your body takes energy from the food. You to cycling: your muscles push the pedals and the cycle moves.
hints: Invite them to draw the Sun first
Point to what each arrow carries
Prompt: under the first arrow write 'the plant uses ___ to make food'
Assert: each arrow passes energy along, from sunlight to your moving cycle

verified.solverAnswer: Sun light -> plant food -> flour roti -> body energy -> muscles move cycle

items.prompt_en: Tina says, 'In a torch, the electricity goes into the bulb and gets used up there, so it never comes back to the battery.' What's the better idea?
items.prompt_hi: Tina kehti hai, 'Torch mein bijli bulb mein jaakar wahin khatam ho jaati hai, isliye kabhi battery mein wapas nahi aati.' Behtar samajh kya hai?
items.answer: The current flows in a complete loop: from the battery, through the bulb and back to the battery. The bulb turns energy from the battery into light and heat. When the battery's stored energy runs low, the torch gets dim.
acceptable: current ghoom ke wapas aata hai
hints: Ask why a torch needs two connections to the battery
Point to the loop drawn on the circuit picture
Prompt: the current goes round a complete ___; the bulb changes energy into ___
Assert: current circles back to the battery; the energy changes into light and heat

verified.solverAnswer: Current flows in a loop through battery, bulb, back; the battery's stored chemical energy is used up, not current

items.prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin what energy is, using three examples from your home.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki energy kya hoti hai, ghar ki teen misaalon ke saath.
items.answer: Energy is something we cannot see that makes things move, heat up, light up or make sound. Examples: food gives us energy to play; electricity runs the fan and the bulb; sunlight dries clothes; the LPG flame cooks food.
hints: Invite them to start with what energy does
Point to the fan, the bulb and their own lunch
Prompt: energy can't be ___, but we see it ___ things
Assert: energy is invisible but shows itself by moving, heating, lighting and sounding

verified.solverAnswer: Energy lets things move, heat, light; examples fan, cooker, food

items.prompt_en: From last time: name four sources of energy.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: energy ke chaar srot batao.
items.answer: Any four: food, the Sun, wind, flowing water, fuels such as petrol, diesel, LPG, coal and wood, electricity, batteries.
hints: Ask what made the kite, the fan and the runner work
Point to the sky and the river
Prompt: food, the ___, wind and ___ water
Assert: food, sun, wind, flowing water, fuels and electricity are energy sources

verified.solverAnswer: Sun, wind, water, fuels (coal/petrol), food, electricity

workedExample.problem: On a kite-flying day, a boy flies his kite and later eats a til laddoo. Find all the energy at work.
steps: Kite: moving air, the wind, pushes the kite up, so wind energy is at work
The wind itself blows because the Sun heats land and air unevenly
The boy pulling the string uses energy from the food he ate
The laddoo's energy comes from sesame and jaggery, made from plants that used sunlight
So both the kite and the boy are powered, in the end, by the Sun
fadedVersion: Kite: moving air, the ___, pushes the kite up
The wind blows because the ___ heats land and air unevenly

items.answer: Dubai is a little to the west of India and about one and a half hours behind, so it is about 6:30 pm there: early evening. items.answer: The torch is the Sun and the ball is the Earth. The Earth spins once in about 24 hours; the side facing the Sun has day and the side away has night. The Sun does not move around us or hide; the Earth's turning makes it seem to rise in the east and set in the west.

skills.title: Name India's main seasons and the changes in weather, plants and animals in each
Observe and record seasonal changes (trees, birds, insects, clothes, food) in a seasons diary
Explain that seasons come from the tilt of the Earth's axis as it goes around the Sun, not from its distance from the Sun

expectations: India has summer, the monsoon (rainy season), the post-monsoon or autumn, winter and spring; traditionally six ritus are counted.

Plants and animals change with the seasons: many trees shed old leaves and grow new ones, flowers like palash and amaltas bloom at fixed times, frogs appear in the monsoon, and many birds fly in from colder lands for the winter.
Seasons happen because the Earth's axis is tilted as it travels around the Sun once a year: when our half leans towards the Sun, sunlight falls more directly and days are longer, so it is summer.
It is not because the Earth comes closer to the Sun: the Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during our winter.
When it is summer in India, it is winter in places like Australia in the southern half of the Earth.

items.prompt_en: Why should a city that is cutting down a forest think about animals too?
items.prompt_hi: Jo shehar jungle kaat raha hai, use jaanwaron ke baare mein bhi kyon sochna chahiye?
items.answer: Animals depend on the forest for food, water and shelter; it is their home as much as ours. Forests also give everyone clean air and water.
hints: Ask where a hornbill or a deer would go
Point to the food, water and shelter links between the forest and its animals
Prompt: the forest is the animals' ___, and it gives everyone clean ___
Assert: forests are shared homes and shared air and water

verified.solverAnswer: Animals live there; lose homes
verified.note: RESOLVED: stale shared-river hint replaced with forest links.

items.prompt_en: Compare a small pond in a closed garden with the ocean. If a plastic bottle is dropped into each, where might each bottle end up?
items.prompt_hi: Band bageeche ke chhote taalab aur samudra ki tulna karo. Agar dono mein ek-ek plastic bottle gir jaaye, toh har bottle kahaan pahunch sakti hai?
items.answer: In the pond it stays in the pond and harms the life there. In the ocean, currents can carry it thousands of kilometres to other countries' beaches, where it harms sea animals far away.
acceptable: samudra wali bottle door tak jaati hai
hints: Ask whether pond water goes anywhere
Point to ocean currents moving like giant rivers
Prompt: the pond bottle stays ___; the ocean bottle can travel to other ___
Assert: in connected waters, our plastic reaches faraway places

verified.solverAnswer: Pond: stays/near; ocean: drifts far across world

items.prompt_en: A neighbour burns dry leaves and garbage in the lane. Who else is affected besides that neighbour?
items.prompt_hi: Ek padosi gali mein sukhe patte aur kachra jalaate hain. Us padosi ke alaawa aur kis-kis pe asar padta hai?
items.answer: Everyone nearby who breathes the smoke: families, children, elderly people and people with breathing problems, and birds and animals too; the smoke drifts into other homes and streets. Burning plastic is especially harmful.
hints: Ask where the smoke goes after a minute
Point to open windows in the lane
Prompt: the smoke drifts into other ___, so ___ breathe it
Assert: smoke from one fire harms everyone around

verified.solverAnswer: Neighbours, children breathe smoke, whole area air

items.prompt_en: Olive Ridley turtles swim across the ocean to lay eggs on Odisha's beaches. Bright lights and plastic on the beach confuse and harm them. What could a beach town do to share the beach with them?
items.prompt_hi: Olive Ridley kachhue samudra paar karke Odisha ke beach pe ande dene aate hain. Beach ki tez roshni aur plastic unhe bhatkaati aur nuksaan pahunchaati hai. Ek beach shehar unke saath beach baantne ke liye kya kar sakta hai?
items.answer: Switch off or shade bright beach lights during nesting season; keep the beach free of plastic and old nets; protect nesting areas; let volunteers guard the nests and help hatchlings reach the sea; keep fishing boats away from nesting waters.
hints: Ask what baby turtles follow to find the sea at night
Point to the bright lights on the shore
Prompt: the town can switch off bright ___ and clear the ___
Assert: dim lights, clean beaches and guarded nests let people and turtles share the shore

verified.solverAnswer: Switch off bright lights, keep beach clean, protect nests

items.prompt_en: Draw a map with two countries, a river flowing from one into the other, a factory chimney and a flock of birds. Use arrows to show how smoke, dirty water and birds cross the border.
items.prompt_hi: Ek map banao jismein do desh hon, ek nadi jo ek desh se doosre mein behti ho, ek factory ki chimney aur pakshiyon ka jhund. Teer se dikhao ki dhuaan, ganda paani aur pakshi seema kaise paar karte hain.
items.answer: Smoke arrows drift with the wind across the border; the river carries waste downstream into the next country; bird arrows fly both ways; the border line stops none of the arrows.
hints: Invite them to draw the border line first
Point to the wind and the river's flow
Prompt: the border line stops ___ of the arrows
Assert: smoke, water and birds cross borders freely

verified.solverAnswer: Map arrows

items.prompt_en: Chintu says, 'If one town dirties its river, that's only that town's problem.' What's wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Chintu kehta hai, 'Agar koi shehar apni nadi gandi kare, toh ye sirf us shehar ki pareshaani hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Rivers keep flowing: the dirty water reaches the towns, fields and animals downstream and finally the sea, so pollution in one place affects many others.
hints: Ask where the river goes after the town
Point to Village B from before
Prompt: the dirty water flows ___ to other towns and the ___
Assert: a river spreads one town's pollution to many places

verified.solverAnswer: Rivers flow to other towns; pollution travels downstream

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child why the Earth is 'our shared home', with one example of air, one of water and one of an animal.
items.prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki Prithvi 'hamara saanjha ghar' kyon hai, hawa, paani aur kisi jaanwar ki ek-ek misaal dekar.
items.answer: All living things share the Earth's air, water and land. Air: smoke from one place drifts to others. Water: a river carries pollution downstream and across countries. Animals: birds like the Amur falcon fly across many countries and need everyone's protection.
hints: Invite them to start with what everyone breathes
Point to the river map and the bird route
Prompt: smoke travels in the ___, waste travels in the ___, and birds cross ___
Assert: air, water and animals connect us all, so care must be shared

verified.solverAnswer: Shared air, water, animals; actions affect others

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one thing that can carry pollution from one place to another far away.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek cheez batao jo pradooshan ko ek jagah se door doosri jagah le ja sakti hai.
items.answer: Wind or moving air, rivers or flowing water, ocean currents.
hints: Ask what carried the stubble smoke to Delhi
Point to the river and the factory
Prompt: ___ carries smoke and ___ carries dirty water
Assert: wind, rivers and ocean currents carry pollution far away

verified.solverAnswer: Wind (air) or river

workedExample.problem: Smoke from fields in Punjab and Haryana reaches Delhi in November. Explain, step by step, how this happens and why it is everyone's problem.
steps: After the rice harvest, some farmers burn the leftover stubble to clear their fields quickly
The burning makes thick smoke full of tiny particles
In October and November, winds often blow from the north-west towards Delhi
Cold, still air near the ground traps the smoke over the city
So people far away breathe polluted air; pollution does not stay where it starts
Fixing it needs everyone: machines and other uses for the stubble, and cities cutting their own pollution too
