skills.title: List simple actions that care for the Earth: refuse, reduce, reuse and recycle; save water and energy; sort waste; plant and look after trees
Plan and track a small action at home or school, such as a week-long no-plastic challenge
Explain how one person's small actions add up when many people do them, and why refusing and reducing come before recycling

expectations: Small daily actions help: carry a cloth bag and a steel bottle, refuse single-use plastic, save water and electricity, sort waste and compost, walk or cycle, and plant trees and look after them.
Refusing and reducing come before reusing and recycling, because not making waste at all is best; recycling still uses energy and not everything gets recycled.
One person's action looks small, but repeated every day by many people it adds up to a big change, and others copy what they see.
A plan works better when it is specific, tracked on a chart and shared with family or friends.
Burning or burying plastic does not make it go away safely; waste should be sorted and given for recycling.

misconceptions.belief: One person's actions do not matter.
signs: Says 'what difference can I make alone?'
Gives up a habit because others are not doing it

diagnostic.prompt_en: Riya uses a cloth bag instead of one plastic bag every day. Does it make a difference?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Riya roz ek plastic thaili ki jagah kapde ka thaila use karti hai. Kya isse farak padta hai?

options.text: Only if the government tells her to do it
Yes; that is 365 fewer plastic bags each year
No; one person on her own can't change anything

remediation.representation: Multiplier ladder: 1 bag a day, then a year, then a class, then a school, then a city
remediation.moveShape: Child climbs the ladder doing the multiplying; ask at which step it stopped feeling small

misconceptions.belief: Recycling is the best and only answer, so using lots of plastic is fine as long as it goes in the recycling bin.
signs: Buys a new bottle daily and feels fine because it is 'recyclable'
Ranks recycling above refusing

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which is best for the Earth?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dharti ke liye sabse achha kya hai?

options.text: Throw the bottle anywhere; someone will recycle it
Use a new plastic bottle daily and recycle it
Carry a steel bottle and keep refilling it

remediation.representation: Waste ladder: refuse at the top, then reduce, reuse, recycle, with the dump at the bottom
remediation.moveShape: Child places everyday choices on the ladder; ask why the top step makes no waste at all

misconceptions.belief: Planting a tree once is enough; it needs no further care.
signs: Counts saplings planted but never asks how many survived
Forgets to water or protect planted saplings

diagnostic.prompt_en: Your class planted 20 saplings in July. What should happen next?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tumhari class ne July mein 20 paudhe lagaaye. Ab aage kya hona chahiye?

options.text: Water them and guard them until they grow strong
Nothing more; once planted, the job is done
Plant 20 more each week and forget about them

remediation.representation: Sapling survival chart: cared-for versus forgotten saplings after one summer
remediation.moveShape: Predict-then-reveal survival after a summer; set up a watering roster together

misconceptions.belief: Burning or burying plastic makes it go away safely.
signs: Suggests burning a pile of plastic to clean up
Thinks buried plastic turns into soil

diagnostic.prompt_en: There is a pile of plastic waste in the lane. What should be done?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Gali mein plastic ke kachre ka dher pada hai. Kya karna chahiye?

options.text: Burn it so that it disappears from the lane
Sort it and give it to the kabadiwala to recycle
Bury it in the garden so it turns into soil

remediation.representation: Two outcome cards: burning sends poisonous smoke into everyone's lungs; burying leaves plastic unchanged for years
remediation.moveShape: Recall the buried-wrapper observation; ask where the plastic goes in each choice

items.prompt_en: Name four things you can do this week to care for the Earth.
items.prompt_hi: Chaar kaam batao jo tum is hafte dharti ki dekhbhaal ke liye kar sakte ho.
items.answer: Any four: carry a cloth bag, use a steel bottle, say no to plastic straws and wrappers, close taps while brushing, switch off lights and fans, sort wet and dry waste, walk or cycle, water a plant or sapling.
hints: Ask what they used today that they could swap
Point to the tap, the switch and the shopping bag
Prompt: I can carry a ___ bag and switch ___ the fan
Assert: small swaps with bags, bottles, taps, switches and waste all help

verified.solverAnswer: Cloth bag, save water, plant tree, switch off, segregate

items.prompt_en: Put these in order from best to least good for the Earth: recycle a plastic bottle; refuse a plastic bottle and carry your own; reuse a plastic bottle as a planter.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe dharti ke liye sabse achhe se kam achhe ke kram mein lagao: plastic bottle recycle karna; plastic bottle lena hi mana karke apni bottle le jaana; plastic bottle ko gamla bana ke dobara use karna.
items.answer: Refuse it and carry your own, then reuse it as a planter, then recycle it. Not making waste comes first, then reusing, then recycling.
hints: Ask which choice makes no waste at all
Point to the waste ladder
Prompt: first ___, then reuse, then ___
Assert: refuse beats reuse, and reuse beats recycle

verified.solverAnswer: Refuse > reuse > recycle

items.prompt_en: Predict first: if each of the 40 students in your class uses a cloth bag instead of one plastic bag every day for a year, about how many plastic bags are saved: about 400, about 4,000 or about 14,000? Then work it out.
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo: agar tumhari class ke 40 bachche saal bhar roz ek plastic thaili ki jagah kapde ka thaila use karein, toh lagbhag kitni plastic thailiyaan bachengi: lagbhag 400, lagbhag 4,000 ya lagbhag 14,000? Phir hisaab lagao.
items.answer: 40 times 365 is 14,600, so about 14,000 bags or more in a year.
hints: Ask for a guess before calculating
Point to 365 days in a year
Prompt: 40 times 365 is ___
Assert: 14,600 bags; one class's small habit saves thousands

items.prompt_en: Keep a bucket under the tap while you brush your teeth with the tap running for 2 minutes, then use that water for plants. Before you start, predict: will the bucket collect about one mug, or many mugs?
items.prompt_hi: Brush karte waqt 2 minute tak nal khula chhodo aur neeche baalti rakho, phir woh paani paudhon mein daal dena. Shuru karne se pehle guess karo: baalti mein lagbhag ek mug paani jama hoga, ya kai mug?
items.answer: Usually many mugs, often several litres, while brushing with the tap closed and one mug of water needs only about one mug.
hints: Ask for a guess before turning on the tap
Point to how fast water rushes from an open tap
Prompt: an open tap for 2 minutes fills ___ mugs, but a closed tap needs only ___
Assert: a running tap wastes litres; one mug is enough for brushing

verified.solverAnswer: Many mugs (about 10+ litres)

items.prompt_en: Two saplings are planted in July in the rains. One gets regular water and a tree guard; the other is planted beside a path where goats graze and then forgotten. Predict which one will still be alive next summer.
items.prompt_hi: July ki baarish mein do paudhe lagaaye gaye. Ek ko roz paani aur tree guard mila; doosra us raaste ke kinaare lagaaya gaya jahaan bakriyaan charti hain, aur phir use bhool gaye. Guess karo agli garmi tak kaunsa zinda rahega.
items.answer: The cared-for one. Saplings need water until their roots grow deep, and protection from animals and trampling; the forgotten one is likely to be eaten or to dry up in summer.
hints: Ask what a goat does when it sees a young plant
Point to the long dry summer ahead
Prompt: a sapling needs ___ and protection until its roots grow ___
Assert: planting is only the start; care decides whether a tree survives

verified.solverAnswer: First one with water and guard

items.prompt_en: Why is 'refuse and reduce' better than 'recycle'?
items.prompt_hi: 'Mana karna aur kam karna' recycle karne se behtar kyon hai?
items.answer: If we do not use the item, no waste is made at all and no materials or energy are used; recycling still uses energy and water, and much plastic never actually gets recycled.
hints: Ask what happens to a bottle that was never bought
Point to the trucks and machines recycling needs
Prompt: refusing makes ___ waste, but recycling still uses ___
Assert: the best waste is the waste never made

verified.solverAnswer: Prevents waste at source; recycling uses energy

items.prompt_en: Why should we never burn plastic or garbage?
items.prompt_hi: Hume plastic ya kachra kabhi kyon nahi jalaana chahiye?
items.answer: Burning plastic gives out poisonous smoke that harms everyone's lungs and pollutes the air; it does not make the waste disappear safely.
hints: Ask where the smoke goes
Point to the neighbours and children breathing it
Prompt: burning plastic makes ___ smoke that harms our ___
Assert: burning turns plastic into poisonous air; sort it for recycling instead

verified.solverAnswer: Toxic smoke, harmful to lungs and air

items.prompt_en: Compare two plans. Plan A: 'I will be good to the Earth.' Plan B: 'For 7 days I will carry a cloth bag and a steel bottle, and tick a chart every evening.' Which is more likely to work, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Do plan ki tulna karo. Plan A: 'Main dharti ke liye achha banunga.' Plan B: '7 din tak main kapde ka thaila aur steel ki bottle le jaaunga, aur roz shaam chart pe tick karunga.' Kaunsa plan zyada kaam karega, aur kyon?
items.answer: Plan B: it is specific and small, has a time limit and a way to check progress; Plan A is vague, so it is easy to forget.
hints: Ask how you would know on day 3 whether Plan A is working
Point to the chart and the 7 days
Prompt: Plan B says exactly ___ to do and how to ___ it
Assert: specific, time-bound, tracked plans work better than vague promises

verified.solverAnswer: Plan B specific, measurable

items.prompt_en: There is a birthday party at your home. Suggest three ways to make it low-waste.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar pe birthday party hai. Ise kam kachre wali banaane ke teen tareeke batao.
items.answer: Any three: steel plates and glasses or leaf plates instead of plastic; no balloons or plastic decorations, or decorations that can be reused; return gifts without plastic packing; sort waste into wet and dry; compost the leftovers; ask guests to bring their own bottles.
hints: Ask what usually fills the bin after a party
Point to plates, cups and decorations
Prompt: use ___ plates instead of plastic and reuse ___
Assert: reusable plates, reusable decorations and sorted waste make a low-waste party

verified.solverAnswer: Cloth/steel plates, no balloons/plastic, return gifts

items.prompt_en: Your colony has 200 homes. If each home saves 10 litres of water a day by closing taps while brushing and washing, how much is saved in 30 days? What could that water be used for?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari colony mein 200 ghar hain. Agar har ghar brush aur haath-muh dhote waqt nal band karke roz 10 litre paani bachaaye, toh 30 din mein kitna paani bachega? Us paani ka kya upyog ho sakta hai?
items.answer: 200 times 10 times 30 is 60,000 litres a month, enough to fill about 3,000 buckets of 20 litres, or several water tankers; it could water gardens and trees or serve families in summer.
hints: Ask for a guess before multiplying
Point to doing it in two steps: per day for the colony, then for the month
Prompt: 200 times 10 is ___ litres a day; times 30 is ___
Assert: 60,000 litres a month from one small habit across 200 homes

verified.solverAnswer: 60,000 litres; for gardens, cleaning, needy

items.prompt_en: Make a 7-day 'no plastic challenge' chart with a row for each day and columns for cloth bag, own bottle and no plastic wrapper. After the week, turn your ticks into a bar graph.
items.prompt_hi: 7 din ka 'no plastic challenge' chart banao: har din ki ek line aur kapde ka thaila, apni bottle aur bina plastic wrapper ke columns. Hafte ke baad apne ticks ko bar graph mein badlo.
items.answer: A chart of days by actions with ticks; a bar graph with one bar per day showing how many plastic-free actions were done; it shows which day or action was hardest and whether things improved.
hints: Invite them to draw the columns first
Point to counting ticks per day for the bars
Prompt: each bar shows how many ___ you did that day
Assert: a chart and graph turn good intentions into something you can see and improve

verified.solverAnswer: Chart and bar graph

items.prompt_en: Bunty says, 'I'm just one kid. Even if I stop using plastic straws, it won't change anything.' What would you tell him?
items.prompt_hi: Bunty kehta hai, 'Main toh bas ek bachcha hoon. Agar main plastic straw chhod bhi doon, toh kuch nahi badlega.' Tum use kya bologe?
items.answer: One child's straws add up to hundreds in a year, and others copy what they see, friends and family; when many people do it, it makes a big difference, and shops change what they sell.
acceptable: jud ke bahut ho jaata hai
hints: Ask how many straws he uses in a year
Point to friends copying a habit
Prompt: one kid's straws in a year are ___, and others ___ what they see
Assert: small actions add up and spread to others

verified.solverAnswer: Small acts add up, others follow

items.prompt_en: Explain to your family your plan to care for the Earth for one week: what you will do, why it matters, and how you will check it.
items.prompt_hi: Apni family ko ek hafte ka dharti bachaao plan samjhao: kya karoge, ye kyon zaroori hai, aur kaise check karoge.
items.answer: Specific actions, such as a cloth bag, a steel bottle, closing taps and sorting waste; why: refusing and reducing make less waste, and small actions add up across many people; checking: a 7-day tick chart reviewed together at the end.
hints: Invite them to name two specific actions first
Point to the waste ladder and the multiplier
Prompt: I will ___, because it makes less ___, and I'll check it with a ___
Assert: specific actions, a reason, and a way to track progress

verified.solverAnswer: Plan: what, why, how check

items.prompt_en: From last time: what do the 3 Rs stand for?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: 3 R ka matlab kya hai?
items.answer: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.
acceptable: kam karo, dobara use karo, recycle karo
hints: Ask what we do before recycling
Point to the waste ladder
Prompt: Reduce, ___, ___
Assert: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle

verified.solverAnswer: Reduce, reuse, recycle
